alt.en: A printed music page numbered 32, headed No. 24 "Oj chanuke, oj chanuke. A chanuke lid" in Latin letters on the left and in Hebrew letters on the right, marked Allegretto and Freilich, with a two-part line for sopranos and altos above a piano part in 2/4 time and four flats, the Yiddish words printed under the notes in Latin letters.
alt.es: Página de música impresa con el número 32 y el encabezado n.º 24 "Oj chanuke, oj chanuke. A chanuke lid" en letras latinas a la izquierda y en letras hebreas a la derecha, marcada Allegretto y Freilich, con una línea a dos voces para sopranos y contraltos sobre una parte de piano en 2/4 y cuatro bemoles, y la letra en ídish impresa bajo las notas en letras latinas.

caption.en: Oy Chanukah as No. 24 in the Society for Jewish Folk Music's Lider-zamelbukh, in the Berlin edition of 1923 that our arrangement is read from: a Hanukkah song, the tune marked "Hasidic", words by M. Rivesman, arranged by P. Lvov.
caption.es: Oy Chanukah como n.º 24 del Lider-zamelbukh de la Sociedad para la Música Popular Judía, en la edición de Berlín de 1923 de la que leemos nuestro arreglo: una canción de Janucá, con la melodía marcada "jasídica", letra de M. Rivesman y arreglo de P. Lvov.

source: Lider-zamelbukh far der yidisher shul un familye, compiled by Z. Kisselgof, arranged by A. Zhitomirsky and P. Lvov, 4th ed. (Berlin: Juwal, [1923]), No. 24, p. 32
library: National Yiddish Book Center (digitized by the Internet Archive)
licenceEvidence: Internet Archive nybc202667 (National Yiddish Book Center), Berlin: Yuval, IA date "[192-?]", Penn Libraries [1923]; the item page states no rights, so PD by age: published in Berlin in the 1920s, so public domain in the US (any 1920s publication is past 95 years by 2026); words M. Rivesman (died 1924), arranger P. Lvov (died 1913), co-arranger A. Zhitomirsky (died 1937), compiler Z. Kisselgof (died 1939), so life plus 70 ended by the end of 2009 in the EU and Israel. A faithful scan of a flat page adds no new copyright. See rights.md.
credit: National Yiddish Book Center, via the Internet Archive

alt.en: A colour print of a wide street lined with tall stone buildings, balconies and shop signs, running straight toward a golden spire on a domed, columned tower in the distance. A green lamp post stands at the right, and high on the corner building at the right a large sign reads "Photographie Martini & Cie".
alt.es: Una impresión en color de una calle ancha bordeada de altos edificios de piedra, balcones y letreros de tiendas, que corre recta hacia una aguja dorada sobre una torre con cúpula y columnas a lo lejos. A la derecha se alza una farola verde, y en lo alto del edificio de la esquina, a la derecha, un gran letrero dice "Photographie Martini & Cie".

caption.en: St Petersburg's Nevsky Prospekt, looking toward the Admiralty, in a photochrom print of the 1890s; in this city Mordkhe Rivesman taught from 1896, and the Society for Jewish Folk Music made the school songbook that is Oy Chanukah's earliest known printing.
caption.es: La avenida Nevski de San Petersburgo, mirando hacia el Almirantazgo, en un fotocromo de la década de 1890; en esta ciudad enseñó Mordkhe Rivesman desde 1896, y la Sociedad para la Música Popular Judía hizo el cancionero escolar que es la impresión más antigua conocida de Oy Chanukah.

source: [The Newsky, (i.e., Nevskii), prospekt and the Admiralty, St. Petersburg, Russia], photochrom print no. "8822" (printed label "S.-Peterburg. Nevskii prospekt i Admiralteistvo"); title from the Detroit Publishing Co. catalogue J, foreign section, 1905; cropped to the buildings and the spire (street level, with its passers-by, and the printed label left out)
library: Library of Congress Prints and Photographs Division, Photochrom Print Collection
licenceEvidence: LoC record https://www.loc.gov/item/2001697493/ (read through the Wayback Machine, 2026-01-12 capture): "Rights Advisory: No known restrictions on reproduction." Photochrom published between ca. 1890 and ca. 1900, anonymous; PD by age in the US, the EU and Israel. See rights.md.
credit: Library of Congress, Prints and Photographs Division, LC-DIG-ppmsc-03885

alt.en: A brass Hanukkah lamp against a dark blue background. Two rearing lions stand on either side of an oval that holds a small branched candlestick, with a crown above the oval, a Star of David above the crown and a single candle cup at the very top. Eight candle cups stand in a row along the base, on short curved feet.
alt.es: Una lámpara de Janucá de latón sobre un fondo azul oscuro. Dos leones erguidos se alzan a cada lado de un óvalo que encierra un pequeño candelabro de brazos, con una corona sobre el óvalo, una estrella de David sobre la corona y un solo portavelas en lo más alto. Ocho portavelas se alinean a lo largo de la base, sobre patas cortas y curvas.

caption.en: A brass Hanukkah lamp labelled Russia, 1890, photographed in 2011 at the National Museum of American Jewish History in Philadelphia: a row of eight cups for the thin little candles that the song tells the children to light.
caption.es: Una lámpara de Janucá de latón con la etiqueta Rusia, 1890, fotografiada en 2011 en el National Museum of American Jewish History de Filadelfia: una hilera de ocho portavelas para las velitas finas que la canción pide a los niños encender.
